title: Console Audit Logs page UX: filters, event detail view, export, empty states, admin-only access
creator: Naomi Feldman
body:
## Context
Enterprise customers are asking for audit log completeness + exportability (SIEM/S3/webhook) and want a usable UI in Console for day-to-day investigations. This design task covers the Console “Audit Logs” page UX including filtering, event list + details, export flow, empty states, and admin-only access handling.

This ticket is tightly coupled to schema v1 (required fields, naming conventions, actor/target model) and the Console backend API (ENG-2493). Design should avoid inventing fields that don’t exist in schema v1 and should assume some payload values may be redacted.

## Goals
- Make audit logs discoverable and usable for security + platform admins.
- Support common workflows:
  1) “Who changed what?” (RBAC / org settings)
  2) “Did a key rotate?” (API key create/rotate/revoke)
  3) “What happened during a rollout?” (deployment/rollout actions)
  4) “Prove to auditor / export to SIEM” (filtered export with clear scope)
- Ensure access control is clear and safe (admin-only) with good UX for non-admin users.

## Non-goals (for v1 page)
- Full-text search across arbitrary JSON payload fields (defer; may be expensive / inconsistent).
- Customer-defined custom schemas or user-configurable columns.
- Reconstructing a complete change timeline across multiple products beyond what audit events provide (we display what’s logged).

## Users / permissions
- Primary: Org admins / Security admins.
- Secondary: Support/TAM during customer calls (read-only, if permitted by customer’s internal roles).

**Access policy assumptions (align w/ RBAC from ENG + rbac-policy-bundle):**
- Default roles: only Admin (and optionally a dedicated “Security Auditor” role if shipped) can view audit logs.
- Export is more privileged than view (may require Admin or explicit “audit.export” permission).
- Non-admin users should not see even partial data (avoid “teaser” rows that could leak information).

## IA / Navigation
- Location: Console → Security & Compliance (or Organization Settings) → Audit Logs.
- Add “Audit Logs” entry gated by permission; if user lacks permission, entry still visible but opens an access-denied state (preferred) OR entry hidden entirely (decision needed; see Open Questions).

## Page layout (v1)
### A) Header
- Title: “Audit Logs”
- Small helper text: retention window (e.g., “Showing last 30 days”) + link to docs (“What’s logged?”)
- Export CTA (primary) aligned right; disabled if no permission.

### B) Filter bar
Keep filters predictable, fast, and aligned with schema fields.

**Proposed filter set:**
1) Time range (required)
   - Presets: Last 1h / 24h / 7d / 30d
   - Custom range (date+time)
2) Event name (typeahead)
   - Suggest based on known registry/naming guidelines (namespace.*)
   - Multi-select
3) Outcome
   - Success / Failure / Unknown
4) Actor
   - Type: User / Service / API key (depending on schema) with ID / email display
   - Input: typeahead for known users + raw string input fallback
5) Target
   - Resource type selector (API key, role, user, deployment, org setting, etc.)
   - ID input
6) Workspace/Project (optional, only if supported by org model)

**Filter UX rules:**
- All filter changes are explicit “Apply” (preferred for performance) OR “auto-apply” with debounce (needs eng input). Current recommendation: explicit Apply to avoid hammering the Audit Logs API and to keep export scope deterministic.
- “Clear all” resets to default time range (Last 24h).
- Show filter chips summary below filter bar for scannability.

### C) Results table
**Columns (v1):**
- Timestamp (absolute + relative on hover)
- Event
- Actor
- Action/Target summary
- Outcome
- Source (optional): Console / API / System (derived from event namespace or actor type)

**Row affordances:**
- Click row opens a right-side details drawer.
- Secondary action in row: “Copy event ID”

**Pagination vs infinite scroll:**
- Prefer pagination with stable cursors (“Next page”) to support export-like workflows and reduce confusion. Infinite scroll can be painful for auditing.

### D) Event details drawer
Show an interpretable summary first, then raw details.

**Top summary section:**
- Event name
- Timestamp
- Outcome + error reason (if failure)
- Actor (display name/email if user; service name if service; API key alias if available)
- Target (resource type + identifier)
- Request correlation
  - request_id
  - trace/span link (if available in Console; otherwise “Copy request ID”)
- IP + user agent (if collected; respect privacy retention/redaction policy)

**Change details (when applicable):**
- For RBAC / settings changes: show “Before → After” diff view if payload includes a diff.
- For dedicated scaling: show desired capacity before/after + initiator (auto/manual).

**Raw JSON section:**
- Collapsible “Raw event JSON” with copy button
- Clearly indicate redaction: show placeholder “(redacted)” and a tooltip explaining why.

## Export UX (v1)
Export should be secure, explicit about scope, and not surprise users.

**Entry points:**
- Main “Export” CTA in header (primary)
- Optional: Export from within filters/results (same flow)

**Modal flow:**
1) Confirm scope
   - Show active filters summary
   - Show estimated number of events (if API can provide)
   - Warn when time range > 7 days (if performance constraints)
2) Destination / format (depends on packaging decision PM-414)
   - For v1 UI: support “Download JSONL/CSV” (if allowed) and/or “Send to configured sink” (S3/webhook/Splunk) if exports are configured.
   - If sinks require prior setup: show “Configure exports” link (admin-only).
3) Run export
   - Async job with progress state
   - Provide “Export history” (may be separate future ticket; for now can be a toast + link to Downloads/Jobs)

**Export guardrails:**
- Require explicit confirmation for very large exports.
- Rate limit messaging (“Exports may take several minutes; you’ll be notified when ready.”)
- If export permission is missing: show disabled CTA with tooltip “Admin permission required to export audit logs.”

## Empty / error states
1) No permission
   - Title: “You don’t have access to Audit Logs”
   - Body: “Audit Logs are restricted to organization administrators.”
   - CTA: “Request access” (opens mailto or internal request flow; needs decision) + secondary “Learn more” link.

2) No results for filters
   - Show empty table state: “No events match these filters”
   - Provide quick actions: “Clear filters” and “Expand time range”.

3) System unavailable / API error
   - Show error banner with retry; include request ID for support.

4) Retention window exceeded
   - If user selects range beyond retention: prevent apply and show inline message: “Audit logs are retained for X days on your plan.”

## Content / terminology
- Prefer “Event” over “Log entry” in UI.
- Use “Outcome: Succeeded/Failed” and include failure reason text from schema (avoid exposing internal stack traces; show sanitized error summary).

## Deliverables
- Figma: Audit Logs page (desktop) + drawer + export modal + 4 empty/error states
- Interaction notes (apply filters, pagination, drawer behavior)
- Component inventory (reuse existing Console table, chip filters, drawers)
- Copy deck (strings) including tooltips and redaction messaging

## Acceptance criteria
- Designs incorporate schema v1 required fields and don’t depend on undefined data.
- At least the following workflows are supported end-to-end:
  - Filter by time + event name + outcome
  - View details including actor/target/request_id
  - Export with clear scope confirmation
  - Non-admin access denied state is implemented in design
- Includes explicit guidance for what to do when IP/user-agent are unavailable or redacted.

## Open questions
1) Navigation behavior for non-admins: hide nav item entirely vs show + access denied screen.
2) Export packaging: will v1 ship download-only, sink-only, or both? (depends on PM-414)
3) Should we include “Environment/Region” filter? Useful for multi-region but may not be reliable in early instrumentation.
4) “Actor” display: do we standardize on email vs user id? (depends on identity model and privacy policy)

## Notes from early eng + security alignment
- No sampling for audit logs.
- Raw payload must be redaction-safe; UI should assume some fields are “(redacted)”.
- Details drawer should not show secrets even if accidentally present; rely on backend redaction, but design should not encourage copying sensitive values.

## Updates / comments
### 2025-06-03 (Felix)
Drafted initial table + drawer layout. Plan to keep filtering explicit with Apply to reduce request volume. Started export modal wireframes.

### 2025-06-06 (Naomi, PM)
Please ensure UI can answer enterprise questionnaires: show schema version somewhere (maybe in details drawer), and make export scope explicit (time range + filters).

### 2025-06-07 (Marcus, Security Eng)
Strong preference for access-denied state (don’t silently hide feature) so customers understand it exists and can request permission.

### 2025-06-10 (Chloe, Eng - Console backend)
Backend can support cursor pagination + basic filters (time, event_name, outcome, actor_id, target_type/target_id). Free-text search won’t be in v1.

### 2025-06-12 (Felix)
Revised filters to match backend constraints: Actor = (user_id/email) input; Target = type + id. Added retention warning copy and “Copy request ID”.

### 2025-06-18 (Allison, Observability)
Please include request_id prominently and a placeholder for trace link integration later. Also add microcopy explaining delivery lag (“Events may appear with up to N minutes delay”).

## Next steps
- Finalize export modal states pending PM-414 packaging decision.
- Design review with Security + Console Eng for access control, retention messaging, and redaction UX.
- Hand-off to ENG-2493 with annotated frames and strings.
